scope: Real Cocos Web/HTML test build; an isolated browser context, not TapTap/device or listening acceptance

stages.name: actual-keyj-engagement-enters-combat
stages.diagnostic: Controlled target only; real keyboard input, damage, GameSession engagement and app-derived music context.

fixture.note: Recovery-held training dummy is non-attacking but remains a genuine threat for the normal engagement rules.

stages.name: natural-settling-starts-aftermath-once
stages.diagnostic: Target removal is a fixture operation; quietSince, actual engagement expiry/settled and the music buffer run naturally.

stages.name: aftermath-mute-and-background-resume
stages.diagnostic: Direct music toggle and app background hooks exercise actual sources; this is not an OS lifecycle test.

stages.name: full-natural-aftermath-tail-returns-to-theme
stages.diagnostic: No near-end seek and no artificial dt advancement; the real 18.46-second phrase plays through its tail, with the explicitly observed mute/background pauses.

stages.name: renewed-combat-interrupts-release-short-lull-does-not-repeat
stages.diagnostic: Only the context contract is overridden; all audio transitions, source playback and stop/fades are real Cocos.

stages.name: title-resets-pending-battle-release
stages.diagnostic: Actual app title/begin actions with diagnostic combat qualification; no new journey or real save is created.

stages.name: death-resets-pending-battle-release
stages.diagnostic: Controlled dead state verifies the app-derived interruption flag, not a normal kill/death scenario.

stages.name: area-change-context-resets-pending-battle-release
stages.diagnostic: Diagnostic areaId transition only; no map assets, traversal or travel/save path is claimed.

stages.name: fight-ending-while-muted-does-not-queue-release
stages.diagnostic: Diagnostic combat/settled context around real source mute/unmute.

limitations: The first transition uses real KeyJ damage and natural engagement/quietSince/settled derivation over a controlled stationary training target.
Removing a controlled target is a fixture operation, not evidence of a normal kill, loot or progression.
Further combat contexts, changed areaId, death state and app background hooks are explicitly diagnostic; no actual OS interruption or map traversal is claimed.
The aftermath runs through its actual 18.46-second musical timeline without near-end seeking or accelerated updates.
Release-only SFX were already verified separately. This probe checks the new music and existing controller, without overwriting old reports.
